answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks using remote enclave attestation at the registration inlet. To join, an agent must present cryptographic quotes signed by secure hardware, binding each identity to distinct physical silicon. An attacker incurs a verifiable cost in dedicated microchips, facing a steep procurement ridge per identity. However, admission queues stall when validation demand reaches its zenith, and the scheme remains vulnerable to physical side-channel exploits.
